items.title: God of War's Kratos & Atreus Officially Return With New Premium Release
items.summary: God of War officially returns with new Kratos and Atreus releases.
items.content:
Image via Sony Santa Monica Add CBR on Google Add as Preferred Source Follow on Google Discover By Emma Singer Published Nov 12, 2026, 9:55 AM EST Emma Singer is an Anime & Gaming Editor from New York with over three years of experience writing about media for CBR. Outside of writing, Emma enjoys doing yoga and playing tennis. Sign in to your CBR account Summary Generate a summary of this story Like Like follow Follow followed Followed Listen Thread Log in Here is a fact-based summary of the story contents: Try something different: Show me the facts Explain it like I’m 5 Give me a lighthearted recap God of War fans have plenty to look forward to moving into 2027, with the release of God of War Laufey quickly approaching, a remake of the classic PS2 trilogy confirmed, and more adventures for Kratos in 2028 and beyond already being planned. However, there's more to the franchise than just its mainline video games.

God of War is no stranger to having merchandise based on it, with God of War Ragnarök, in particular, having created some truly stunning, luxury statues in the image of characters like Atreus and Thor. Now, a new company, one of the biggest in the business, is putting its own spin on Ragnarök, with new releases for Kratos and Atreus.

Close Image via Santa Monica Studio Atreus and Kratos embrace each other Image via Sony Kratos unleashing his fury in God of War Image via Sony and Santa Monica Studios Kratos looking sad in God of War Ragnarok Image via Sony and Santa Monica Studios window.arrayOfGalleries["article-gallery-1-42911617"] = '" Close Image via Santa Monica Studio Atreus and Kratos embrace each other Image via Sony Kratos unleashing his fury in God of War Image via Sony and Santa Monica Studios Kratos looking sad in God of War Ragnarok Image via Sony and Santa Monica Studios "'; Dark Horse Direct, one of the most famous figure and statue makers in the world, has officially announced a collaboration with Santa Monica Studio to create merchandise based on God of War Ragnarök. Unsurprisingly, they've already confirmed that they'll be making high-quality pieces based on the game's two lead characters, Kratos and Atreus.

"We’re excited to announce a new partnership that will bring you collectibles from the world of God of War Ragnarök!" Dark Horse Direct posted on their website on November 9. "From PVC Figures, a premium statue featuring Kratos and Atreus, and much more, there will be plenty to look forward to! "

A waitlist is available to join for fans interested in being notified about product updates, early pre-order access, and exclusive discounts.

Kratos is the longtime protagonist of the God of War franchise, and one of the biggest PlayStation icons ever. Over the decades, he's evolved far more than anyone ever expected, having grown from the vengeful, rage-filled, bloodthirsty anti-hero who slayed the Greek gods in the 2000s, to the older, wiser, relatively more peaceful father figure who formed a family among the Norse gods in the modern era.

Atreus was first introduced in God of War (2018) as the son of Kratos and Faye, before becoming a full playable character in God of War Ragnarök. Also known as Loki Laufeyson, the Norse god of mischief, it's unclear what his role in the series will be as it moves on to a new and exciting pantheon to explore, but he remains a fan-favorite nonetheless, both for his own strengths as a character, and the development and emotions he brings out of Kratos.

Both Kratos and Atreus have already received immensely high-quality statues from Prime 1 Studio , several in the former's case, but these releases have all had price tags of well over $1,000 USD. Hopefully, Dark Horse Direct will be able to offer more budget options, while still maintaining a high standard of quality.

items.title: God of War Ragnarok Leads Sony’s Top-Grossing PS5-Era Games at US$1.4B, per Alinea
items.summary: Alinea Analytics estimates Sony's ten biggest PlayStation Studios games of the PS5 generation grossed over US$6.5B. Ragnarok and Spider-Man 2 lead the list.
items.content:
Kratos is still out-earning everything else Sony has put its name on this generation. God of War Ragnarok sits at the top of a new estimate of the highest-grossing PlayStation Studios games of the PS5 era with about US$1.4 billion in gross revenue. Market research firm Alinea Analytics puts the combined total for the top ten at more than US$6.5 billion.

Alinea published the figures in its newsletter as the PS5 approaches its sixth birthday, and senior analyst Rhys Elliott shared the ranking on X. These are third-party estimates, not numbers from Sony. They’re also gross revenue figures, not profit. Nobody outside Sony knows what Ragnarok cost to make, so the “most profitable” framing that’s been doing the rounds goes further than the data does.

Here’s the full order, according to Alinea’s estimates:

Ragnarok’s total comes from an estimated 21.6 million copies. About 20.1 million of those were sold on PlayStation, with the rest on Steam. It’s also a cross-gen game, and Alinea says 75.2% of its PlayStation copies went to PS5 owners. Roughly 27.5% of those PlayStation sales were physical.

It’s still selling, too. Alinea estimates Ragnarok has moved another 1.1 million copies in 2026, worth around US$60 million, even though it’s been on PS Plus Extra. Spider-Man 2 is close behind on US$1.3 billion. More than US$1.2 billion of that came from PS5, and nearly US$70 million came from Steam.

The argument online is mostly about what the list says, and doesn’t say, about Sony’s live-service push:

Mads ⭐️ @fahrennheit.bsky.social Happy 4th anniversary to one of my favorite games God of War Ragnarok!! 🫶 I did not have anything new prepared to share this year so heres a resharing of some old gow art of mine to celebrate #gow #godofwarragnarok #art 0 replies 5 reposts 13 likes 9 Nov 2026

Sony’s spent a big chunk of this generation chasing ongoing online games. Only one made the cut. Helldivers 2 comes fourth on an estimated US$786.3 million from 23 million copies. Most of those, 66.1%, sold on Steam. PS5 accounts for 25.7%, and the Xbox port that arrived about a year and a half later makes up 8.3%.

Gran Turismo 7 is third with US$841.9 million from 12.7 million copies. That’s the series’ long-tail model doing its job: you keep coming back for new cars and events, and Polyphony keeps adding them. Everything else in the top ten is a story-led single-player game.

Our view: the list makes the case for single-player better than any fan campaign could. The two biggest earners are traditional sequels, and the only true live-service game here came from Arrowhead, an outside studio. Sony’s own live-service projects aren’t on it at all.

PlayStation still does most of the earning. Alinea splits the US$6.5 billion as 84.7% from PlayStation, 14.1% from Steam and 1.2% from Xbox, and that Xbox share comes entirely from Helldivers 2.

Stellar Blade tells a more interesting PC story. Shift Up’s action game earned 59.7% of its US$316.9 million on PS5, but copies split almost evenly. PlayStation has 50.4% of its estimated 5.4 million copies and Steam has 49.6%, even though the PC version launched a year later. Like Helldivers 2, it was published by Sony but made by an outside studio.

Read also: Stellar Blade’s Bayonetta Outfits Got Quick Approval as PlatinumGames Stayed Hands-Off

Two entries stand out for how quickly they got here. Ghost of Yotei launched in October 2025 and is already sixth, with an estimated US$410.1 million from 5.5 million copies, all on PS5. Alinea says a recent content update gave it a fresh bump.

items.title: God of War: Ragnarok is reportedly the highest-earning PlayStation Studios game this generation, but Marvel's Spider-Man 2 isn't far behind
items.summary: God of War: Ragnarok and Marvel's Spider-Man 2 are the best-selling PlayStation Studios games this generation, according to one analyst.
items.content:
Image credit: Sony News by Kaan Serin Contributor Published on Nov. 9, 2026, 7:02 p.m. 22 comments Follow Astro Bot Prioritise us on Google God of War: Ragnarok is the generation's best-selling and highest-earning PlayStation Studios game, according to a new report, but the full top 10 list has a few nice surprises.

In the four years since its PS5 release and two years since its PC port, God of War: Ragnarok has reportedly sold just over 20m copies and generated $1.4b in revenue, according to estimates from Alinea Analytics . About 27.5 percent of the 15m copies it sold on console came from physical editions, and the action blockbuster apparently sold a further 1.1m this year alone. Not bad, boy.

Those stats should bode well for the series' next romp God of War: Laufey - which sees Faye take the spotlight across a multi-mythological afterlife and was recently delayed into May 2027 - even if PlayStation moves away from PC ports for its signature single-player games.

Kratos and Atreus only narrowly beat out perhaps the biggest superhero of them all: Marvel's Spider-Man 2 , a game that reportedly made a whopping $1.3b off 19.1m copies across PS5 and PC. The Spidey sequel should keep swinging even higher as the years chug on, though - the report states that sales always surge during the holiday months, and this year's big screen behemoth Spider-Man: Brand New Day led to an even bigger spike than usual.

Racing sim royalty Gran Turismo 7 ($841m), bug-squashing phenomenon Helldivers 2 ($786m), robo-dino sequel Horizon: Forbidden West ($485m), vengeful spirit sim Ghost of Yotei ($410m), undead remake The Last of Us Part 1 ($341m), multidimensional romp Ratchet and Clank: Rift Apart ($334m), Stellar Blade ($316m) and delightful throwback Astro Bot ($292m) round out the top 10 games published by PlayStation Studios this generation.

It's worth noting that Helldivers 2 and Stellar Blade were developed by studios outside the PlayStation umbrella, but the console maker still published both upon release. Ghost of Yotei's performance is also particularly impressive since Sucker Punch's sequel has only been out for a year and didn't get the benefit of a PC port, like many of its PS5 siblings. The success couldn't save Sucker Punch from recent layoffs , however.

On PlayStation's decision to kill disc-based physical releases , analyst Rhys Elliott said that the bottom five games in the list together made $281.7m this year alone: "PlayStation wants those numbers to be bigger in the coming years, which is one of the reasons it's killing the disc (alongside the better margins it and publishers get through digital.)"

items.title: God of War Ragnarok Tops List of 10 Highest-Grossing PlayStation Studios Games From the PS5 Generation
items.summary: Sony Santa Monica Studios' God of War Ragnarok tops the list of highest-grossing PlayStation Studios games of the PS5 generation, according to Alinea Analytics.
items.content:
Sony Santa Monica Studios' God of War Ragnarok tops the list of highest-grossing PlayStation Studios games of the PS5 generation, according to Alinea Analytics.

The game data company's head of market analysis, Rhys Elliott, shared information related to sales for titles published under the PlayStation banner in a Substack post today. It features a list of 10 games estimated to have emerged as Sony's best performers so far.

You can probably guess at least some of the games that managed to crack the top 10 list, but there are a few interesting inclusions in there, too. God of War Ragnarok, for example, is placed at number one with an estimated $1.4 billion in gross revenue. Spider-Man 2 is second at $1.3 billion, with Gran Turismo 7 placed third at $841.9 million. You can see the full list below.

Here's the 10 top-grossing PlayStation Studios games of this generation (@alineaanalytics estimates). Together, the 10 games generated over $6.5 billion across PlayStation (84.7%), Steam (14.1%), and Xbox (1.2% via just Helldivers 2). Full write-up over on Substack. https://t.co/3XLgJdTqUM

8. Ratchet & Clank: Rift Apart – $334.9 million

These 10 games alone have generated $6.5 billion for PlayStation. Although the list only includes titles from the PS5 generation, the numbers here do account for other platforms. Astro Bot, for example, is exclusive to PS5 and earned its amount only through the estimated 4.7 million copies it sold on that platform.

God of War Ragnarok, meanwhile, is also available on PS4 and PC, with Alinea Analytics' breakdown showing its revenue accumulated via 21.6 million copies across all three platforms. Of its performance on PlayStation, 75.2% of its 20.1 million share of copies sold were on PS5, specifically, with 27.5% of all sales on PS4 and PS5 being physical. Elliott called the Norse God of War sequel an evergreen title for Sony, explaining that in 2026 alone it's managed to sell 1.1 million copies. That's an impressive feat compared even to brand-new games from this year, and it's only more impressive when you consider that it was made accessible to PlayStation Extra subscribers nearly two years ago in January of 2025. Alinea Analytics estimates show that 6.7 million PlayStation Plus users have accessed it via the service.

Ghost of Yōtei may have technically been trailing behind its predecessor as of October , but at least for now, its recent Echoes of Sekigahara expansion has helped it land in sixth. As of today's update, it's said to have sold 5.5 million copies as a PS5 exclusive. Another interesting addition from the list is Stellar Blade, which is technically a second-party release published by PlayStation Studios. Today's data accounts for sales across PS5 and Steam (a Nintendo Switch 2 version launched yesterday) and shows that 59.7% of its revenue was earned from the former and 40.3% from the latter.

Alinea Analytics' breakdown is not an official look into where sales are at with Sony's gaming division. Meanwhile, its update follows official information released by the PlayStation company just earlier this week. It came with the news that it had raised its sales forecast while also sharing figures for Marvel's Wolverine for the first time . For more, you can see how PlayStation's Bloodborne has held up in the 11 years since its launch on PS4 .

Michael Cripe is a freelance writer with IGN. He's best known for his work at sites like The Pitch, The Escapist, and OnlySP. Be sure to give him a follow on Bluesky (@mikecripe.bsky.social) and Twitter (@MikeCripe).

items.title: God Of War Ragnarok Is The Biggest First-Party PlayStation Game This Generation, Claims Market Analyst
items.summary: A market analyst has shared new data that reveals God of War Ragnarok is PlayStation's most successful first-party title this generation.
items.content:
Alinea Analytics’ Rhys Elliot has revealed on X that God of War Ragnarok has achieved 21.6 million copies on PlayStation and Steam, generating $1.4 billion in gross revenue — making it PlayStation’s most successful first-party title of the generation.

The analyst also offered details as to why God of War Ragnaork was able to top Marvel’s Spider-Man 2, a game that has huge crossover appeal given that it’s based on a franchise that has massive reach across avenues such as film and comic books. Elliot noted that Marvel’s Spider-Man 2 is a PS5 console exclusive, while God of War Ragnarok is also available for PS4, so Insomniac Games’ sequel misses out on a large install base.

It’s another PlayStation evergreen seller, too. This year, Ragnarok has already sold 1.1M copies, generating nearly $60M (68% on PlayStation), outperforming new 2026 titles like Gears of War E-Day and Saros Overall, Ragnarok has been accessed by 6.7M PlayStation Plus players (it was added to the Extra tier about two years ago). So it’s performed that well this year DESPITE subscription cannibalisation. That’s the pull of God of War IP.

God of War Ragnarok was released for PS5 & PS4 in November 2022, and is the sequel to God of War (2018), and finds Atreus and Kratos navigating the harsh conditions left by the three-year period of Fimbulwinter in Midgard. Unlike the previous game however, all nine realms can be visited by the duo, as they fight against a new range of enemies in order to prevent Ragnarok, which seems them coming into contact with Norse gods such as Thor and Odin. You can read our review here .

God Of War: Sons of Sparta PS4 has been officially confirmed by Sony Santa Monica Studio. Get full details here.

items.title: All Of The God Of War Games, Ranked From Worst To Best
items.summary: Before God of War Laufey takes us on Faye’s journey, let’s look back at the ups and downs of Kratos’
items.content:
God of War is about to do something it hasn’t done before: center someone other than Kratos. Before we head into the Everywhen as Faye with God of War Laufey , we thought we’d take a look back at over 20 years of god-slaying and navigating Kratos’ dysfunctional family tree by ranking all the previous games from worst to best. Don’t yell at us if your fave is low on the list. Simply swear vengeance upon us and take out a pantheon of gods on the way.

Mechanically, the 2D, sidescrolling Sons of Sparta maybe wasn’t the kind of treatment I want God of War to get but narratively, yes, please, may I have another. I thought turning GOW into a metroidvania was cute, but the gameplay got tedious after a while. However, I adored that the narrative conceit of the game is Kratos telling his daughter Calliope a story about his life as a child. I have so much grief for Kratos’ first family because they wield so much narrative power over this entire franchise but we know so little about them. Regardless of the gameplay, I’m glad Sons of Sparta exists so I can get my “Kratos being a good dad to his FIRST child for a change” fix. — Ash Parrish

The last PS3 God of War is absolutely a relic of a pre-live-service era when companies were bolting multiplayer modes onto the sides of their most lucrative ships, so it’s not super surprising that the bulk of Ascension feels a little underbaked. The prequel is still full of the kinds of incredible, cinematic set pieces and twitchy action that make each God of War at least memorable, but its hack-and-slash combat feels narrowly focused on Kratos’ iconic Blades of Chaos, with you shifting between different elemental affinities instead of different weapons that would have more tangibly changed up your playstyle and the flow of combat. That final boss fight against the Kraken and the Furies still whips pretty hard, though. — Kenneth Shepard

God of War Ragnarok would have been incredible as two games instead of one. Yeah, the frustratingly bloated and overly long sequel is still rock solid, with fantastic action and some incredible moments, especially for Kratos and Atreus, who remain the heart and soul of the series’ Norse mythology games despite the ever-expanding cast. Still, it’s hard to not get wistful thinking of what this story might’ve looked like if it’d had a bit of breathing room. Ragnarok ’s Valhalla DLC, meanwhile, shows exactly what a hypothetical scaled-back sequel could have looked like by giving Kratos a roguelike therapy session that’s laser-focused on one character instead of a dozen, which helps the core action mechanics shine through in a way that base Ragnarok didn’t, having a bit too much noise going on to let that action sing sometimes. It’s a shame because so many of Ragnarok ’s narrative threads, such as Angrboda seeking out the remnants of the frost giants and the inner machinations of Thor’s family drama, are genuinely compelling, but it’s all fighting for attention in a game that’s trying to wrap up a trilogy’s-worth of stories in a second game. — Kenneth Shepard

The PlayStation Portable was one of the earlier attempts at a handheld offering console-level experiences, and God of War: Chains of Olympus was certainly one of the best examples of a studio making it happen. Ready at Dawn pulled off a handheld God of War remarkably well, creating a Kratos experience that was pretty comparable to its console brethren and that you could take on the go. Though it isn’t quite as narratively illuminating as its sequel, it’s still a truly impressive feat for 2008. — Kenneth Shepard

Ghost of Sparta , Ready at Dawn’s second Chaos Blade swing at a handheld God of War game, is just as solid a game as its predecessor. What gives it a bit of an edge over Chains of Olympus is how much we learn about Kratos in the prequel, including the introduction of his brother Deimos, who adds a whole new wrinkle to Kratos’ dysfunctional family tree. That guy is an onion of layers to peel back, and Ready at Dawn was cooking every time it got the keys to the kitchen. — Kenneth Shepard

Remembering the original God of War 21 years after its 2005 launch feels quaint in a way that makes me uncomfortable with my advancing age. I remember when this game came out; I played it then. But viewing this game now, in the context of what the series has grown into, is bewildering. Voiced by T.C. Carson and equipped with a double jump, this Kratos is a completely different person in a completely different type of game. OG God of War bleeds mid-aughts edginess. The game’s opening shot features a morose Kratos yeeting himself off a cliff, and every female character has her breasts out, just because. That said, the original God of War was a great action platformer with the kind of bloody, violent combat we craved in the mid-aughts. — Ash Parrish

God of War III felt big enough to shoulder the weight of being the “last” major game in the franchise at the time. It contained a “resolution” to Kratos’ story that featured some pretty interesting commentary on the nature and purpose of hope, even if it wasn’t executed that well. God of War III is the franchise’s first flirtation with the “Give Kratos a lil guy to look after” mechanic as Pandora, she of the famous box, tags along for part of your adventure. Chatty sidekicks who help you open doors were already a thing by the time this game came out in 2010, but I wasn’t sure how well the famously dour Kratos would work with the bright and chipper Pandora. And y’know what, he did pretty good. There’s a moment when Zeus hurts Pandora and the camera cuts to Kratos who’s wearing the biggest, ugliest frown, as though all the sliders on his face model were cranked all the way down, and I believed it. I was on his side. — Ash Parrish

God of War II improves on the original in every way with a bigger story and bloodier combat. I really enjoyed the smart, narrative way the game depowers Kratos to set him up to receive new weapons and abilities. Fighting the Colossus of Rhodes, the opening battle in God of War II , is one of the greater gameplay sequences of the PS2 era. Incredibly cinematic and bombastic— you’re fighting the Greek mythological equivalent of a Gundam after all— the fight really conveys what a godly struggle should be, a neat escalation of the mortal battles of the first game. — Ash Parrish

God of War ’s Norse-themed reboot was risky. It changed everything we knew about what it meant to embody Kratos, primarily by acting as a metatextual critique of what the series had once been. A somber, shame-ridden Kratos has retreated to the Nine Realms after slaughtering the Greek pantheon, and rather than flaunting those acts, he attempts to hide them away from his son Atreus before confronting his past and choosing to believe that how things have been is not how they must be. The original God of War games were very much of a different era, one in which edgy, violent excess sold copies. As tastes have changed, God of War had to as well if it was going to thrive, and the 2018 reboot does so not by pretending what came before didn’t happen, but instead by using Kratos’ decade of rage as a springboard to become something greater.

And boy, did it become something greater on the mechanical front, too. Kratos trades his Blades of Chaos (initially) for an icy Leviathan Axe that makes the game feel heavier and more challenging, and the series adopts RPG-lite elements to offer more chances for player expression than the original games were ever capable of. With this reboot, Santa Monica Studio sought to reinvent everything God of War ever was, from its ethos to its best-in-class combat, and it succeeded. — Kenneth Shepard

Find Kyle on Letterboxd: KyleG5 Sign in to your ScreenRant account Like Like follow Follow followed Followed Thread 1 Log in Here is a fact-based summary of the story contents: Try something different: Show me the facts Explain it like I’m 5 Give me a lighthearted recap A God of War Ragnarök sequel has been rumored to be in development for some time, but newly uncovered game files potentially lay out the next game's story setup. Ragnarök 's finale is still the chronological end-point for the franchise so far, with newly released Sons of Sparta taking us all the way back to Kratos' childhood in Greece. Unused dialog now found in Ragnarök seems to support the rumors that the series' next entry will involve the Ancient Egyptian pantheon.

The scenes uncovered by Reddit user TheMorse_ show a couple of conversations that seem to set up Kratos and Atreus' arrival in Egypt. The most overt hint is Atreus' traveling companion, a character named Mau, who may be the cat god from Egyptian mythology, a form taken on by the sun god Ra. Athena also appears in the files, hinting at a continued overarching story. A similar discovery was made in the God of War (2018) files, which included Ragnarök 's beginning, lending credence to the idea that the next game's intro has been found.

Atreus' conversation with Mau is one-sided, since Mau can only speak its name (like a cat meowing), so it doesn't offer many details. It implies the two were traveling to a specific destination, with Atreus' lines concluding, " Sounds like we found it ." Athena appears in the files alongside a robed figure, though TheMorse_ believes they are one and the same, with Athena being the robed figure before her identity is revealed.

[Warning: Spoilers for God of War Ragnarök below.]

The robed figure first speaks in Greek: " To lefkó fídi tha se fáei ," which translates to " The white snake will eat you ." In English, the robed figure then says, " One failed us. One rejected us ," to which Athena replies (or continues), " We have a problem ." The leading theory is that the conversation is about Odin, who failed to use a mask in Ragnarök which would grant endless knowledge, and Atreus, who rejected the opportunity to use the mask.

Such a scene would follow up on a vision Kratos has of Athena in 2018's God of War , where she appears as he retrieves the Blades of Chaos. It's left up to interpretation whether this vision was in Kratos' own mind, or if Athena actually manifested in some form. Athena played a sort of puppet master role in the original God of War Greek saga, and seems to be in league with beings of an order even higher than the Greek and Norse pantheons.

Kratos standing on a beach in God of War Ragnarok. This datamine is perhaps the most concrete evidence so far that God of War will go to Egypt, but the setting has been suspected for quite some time. Last year, it was rumored that two new God of War games were in development. One turned out to be Sons of Sparta , while the other is presumably the next mainline installment that will continue Kratos and Atreus' story. At the time, the recently announced God of War Trilogy Remake was not suspected.

Further rumors have honed in on an Egyptian setting, which has long been suspected to host a new saga, and is a setting highly requested by fans. Supposed details on the game include Kratos acquiring an Egyptian sword, likely a khopesh, and that it will not necessarily star Atreus as the main playable character, who was, in some ways, set up to take the reins in Ragnarök .

Mau's name in the unused Ragnarök dialog is the most tangible connection to Egypt, but the " white snake " referenced by the robed figure is suspected to be Ouroboros (though snakes are very common in ancient mythologies). The snake consuming its own tail is a motif found in numerous ancient mythologies, but has appeared earliest in archaeological discoveries from Egypt. All things considered, it's looking very likely that a God of War Ragnarök sequel is underway at Santa Monica Studio, and evidence that the franchise is heading to Ancient Egypt is mounting.

items.title: God of War Sons of Sparta: new content and PS4 version arrive November 16
items.summary: Get ready to race the clock in Hermes Mode and survive the lethal Erebus Mode.
items.content:
20 0 168 Like this Get ready to race the clock in Hermes Mode and survive the lethal Erebus Mode.

Updated (November 13, 2026): We’re thrilled to announce that God of War Sons of Sparta is coming to the PlayStation 4 on November 16 at midnight local time!

In addition to bringing the game to PS4 players, Mega Cat Studios will also be releasing a patch at the same time introducing two new modes that will be available for both PS4 and PS5 consoles.

Hermes Mode: Race against the clock with a dedicated speedrunning toolkit with a split-based timer, persistent scoreboard, and more. You can access Hermes Mode after you beat the game for the first time or by entering the following code in the start menu: Up, Up, Down, Down, Left, Right, Left, Right, L1, R1, Touchpad.

Erebus Mode: Take on the ultimate challenge where both you and your enemies fall in a single hit.

Your game mode can be selected upon starting a new game and selecting a save slot. Please note that once selected, the game mode chosen for that save file cannot be changed.

We hope everyone enjoys journeying across Greece with Kratos and Deimos!

Original Story: God of War Sons of Sparta is a brand-new entry to the series available now for the PlayStation 5!

Developed by our partners at Mega Cat Studios, Sons of Sparta takes God of War staples and translates them like never before into a retro-inspired 2D action platformer.

Looking to learn more before embarking on a journey back to ancient Greece this weekend? Here’s what you need to know about God of War Sons of Sparta!

Sons of Sparta is a canon story that takes place in Kratos’ youth from the writing team that brought you God of War (2018), God of War Ragnarök, and God of War Ragnarök: Valhalla.

Set during the brutal training period Spartan cadets undergo at the Agoge – Kratos, alongside his brother Deimos, must traverse far beyond the home they know into the beautiful yet dangerous region of Laconia that surrounds the familiar walls of Sparta.

Kratos and Deimos must overcome threats that will put all their training to the test while challenging them to confront the true meaning of duty, honor, and brotherhood.

Play Video Heartfelt performances Sons of Sparta features a fantastic vocal cast whose performances bring the depth and emotion fans expect from God of War games.

items.content:
• Add more error checking and logging for NVIDIA Streamline

  • When NVIDIAStreamlineLog enabled, a log file in the Save Game directory will be generated and overwritten every launch. If encountering errors, please submit a support ticket including this log. C:\Users\\Saved Games\God of War Ragnarök\sl.log

items.title: Black Screen Launch Issue Hotfix
items.summary: An NVIDIA Driver Crash/Soft Lock that prevents the game from loading is under investigation. In the meantime, we've implemented a work around for the cause of the crash to change how shader compilation works. This change may cause some micr
items.content:
An NVIDIA Driver Crash/Soft Lock that prevents the game from loading is under investigation. In the meantime, we've implemented a work around for the cause of the crash to change how shader compilation works. This change may cause some micro-stuttering during initial load, but will hopefully avoid the driver crash that prevents game from starting.

Please verify files after patching.

items.title: Patch 9 - 20th Anniversary Update
items.summary: As a gift to everyone who owns God of War Ragnarök, the Dark Odyssey collection is now available in-game at no additional cost! Inspired by the working name of God of War (2005) and the skin that originally appeared in God of War II as a re
items.content:
As a gift to everyone who owns God of War Ragnarök, the Dark Odyssey collection is now available in-game at no additional cost! Inspired by the working name of God of War (2005) and the skin that originally appeared in God of War II as a reward for beating the game on God Mode difficulty, we have brought back the black and gold theme for the anniversary.

Dark Odyssey Collection

Dark Odyssey Armor & Appearance for Kratos
  • Dark Odyssey Kratos Appearance
  • Dark Odyssey Armor Set for Kratos (Dark Odyssey Breastplate, Dark Odyssey Bracers, Dark Odyssey Belt)
Dark Odyssey Companion Armor
  • Dark Odyssey Vestment for Atreus
  • Dark Odyssey Witch Frock for Freya
Dark Odyssey Weapon Appearances & Attachments*
  • Dark Odyssey Leviathan Axe & Dark Odyssey Knob
  • Dark Odyssey Blades of Chaos & Dark Odyssey Handles
  • Dark Odyssey Draupnir Spear & Dark Odyssey Hind
Dark Odyssey Shield Appearances & Rönd
  • Dark Odyssey Guardian Shield
  • Dark Odyssey Dauntless Shield
  • Dark Odyssey Stone Wall Shield
  • Dark Odyssey Shatter Start Shield
  • Dark Odyssey Onslaught Shield
  • Dark Odyssey Spartan Aspis Shield
  • Dark Odyssey Rönd
*Please note, the weapon appearances are made for the fully upgraded version of each weapon and will only be available for use upon reaching that upgrade.

Edit Appearance for Weapon & Shield Attachments

With the addition of the new Dark Odyssey weapon attachments and shield rönd in the patch, we have added the ability to use the ‘Edit Appearance’ feature on those components of Kratos’ arsenal. You’ll be able to pick whatever visual suits your look with the functionality you want for your build!
